Montech is battling rising PC build costs by targeting the budget end of PC building with its new cases. At Computex 2026, the company is rolling-out the Montech TG3 for $60, the King 95 3D, and the F738 ATX cases, alongside some new fans. As part of this coverage, we invited Montech's product manager to join us for an educational discussion about manufacturing tools, equipment, and pricing.

In this hardware news recap, we talk plans for Computex, AI companies getting booed at commencement speeches, NVIDIA's vibecoded drivers striking again with security vulnerabilities (but at least they're patched), RAM companies taking on debt to buy supply, and more. The memory situation in particular is concerning, as RAM module makers taking debt means consumers will pay for that debt and interest in retail prices, driving them up further.

Watch our recent documentary about the collapse of the consumer PC industry here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zyQwAhppWj8
